text:
Happy Veterans Day evening. We're sitting in the mid 40s under a lid of cloud, and sunset is at 4:29, so don't expect any color. It'll just fade to gray. Tonight stays mostly cloudy and quiet, with the temperature sliding to around 31 by morning, so bundle up a bit if you're out late.

Thursday is the wet one. Rain moves in around 10 in the morning and is steadiest from about noon to 4, with a high near 43. It doesn't look like much, about a tenth of an inch, but the European model and ICON are wetter than the official forecast, so I'd carry the umbrella and plan outdoor errands for the morning. As it cools Thursday night, the rain turns to a rain and snow mix, with the best chance of flakes in the small hours Friday. The ground is still too warm for anything to stick in town, so expect wet pavement rather than a shoveling job. Friday brightens up a touch but stays chilly, in the low 40s.

week.blurb: Mostly cloudy and chilly for Veterans Day, a high near 46 and dry, dropping to around 31 tonight.
Rain and snow mix moving in after 7am, light with under a tenth of an inch, high near 43, turning more wintry tonight.
Cloudy and raw, high near 41 with a few rain and snow flakes around midday, barely a dusting at most, and a breezy north wind.
Mostly cloudy and breezy, high near 42, with a coin-flip chance of a rain and snow mix, so keep the jacket handy.
A little rain early, then maybe a flurry or mixed shower by midday, high near 43, with the odds trending lower.
Looks like a drier start to the week, partly sunny and a bit chilly with a high near 43 and a cold night.
Mostly sunny and the pick of the week, with a high near 45 and a light wind, if the pattern holds.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-11-11T20:13:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. A coastal low will bring widespread lower elevation rain and wet snow mainly above 1200 feet with shower chances continuing through the weekend.
  2. A few lingering showers Sunday, then high confidence in dry weather early next week.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 242 PM EST Wednesday... A Winter Weather Advisory has been issued for the higher terrain of the Adirondacks and portions of the southern Green Mountains for Thursday and early Friday.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Model consensus continues to favor a coastal type low to deepen and wrap moisture back across Vermont and northern New York Thursday with a more upslope regime developing by Friday. Temperatures and this pattern support lower elevation rain Thursday and mainly higher elevation snowfall before temperatures drop Thursday night promoting snow showers to most valley floors. The overall forecast remains quite tricky with balancing QPF timing, changing SLRs, and a shift in primary precipitation mechanisms while models struggle with the details. Where the models continue to struggle are placement of the surface circulation, extent of northward moisture transport and QPF amounts, and amount of cold air in place across the region. The latest trends have pushed moisture back southward leaving more modest QPF across northern New York and Vermont representing nearly a 50% reduction to QPF from the previous forecast for many locations. As such, snow totals were decreased with most spots only seeing a dusting to around 1 inch, southern and Adirondack locations below 1200 feet receiving 1-2 inches, and 2-5 inches above 1200ft. This will primarily be a function of the period of heaviest precipitation period occurring over the daytime hours with snow ratios being lower due to thermal profiles. As such, snow will start at higher elevations and crash down to around 1000 feet over the evening hours as the low pulls away. The upslope regime begins Thursday night and continues through early Friday with higher snow ratios supporting more efficient accumulation rates, but hindered by decreasing moisture. Cooling profiles and dynamic cooling processes will help snow reach most valley locations overnight Thursday night and early Friday. However, it will be tough to get snow accumulations in lower valleys like the Champlain Valley given the relatively warm ground temperatures likely melting most, if not all, of the snow that reaches the ground Thursday night. For the St Lawrence Valley, most of the moisture will have exited before temperature profiles cool enough to allow snow to occur. Behind the coastal low, northerly flow will remain through Saturday keeping shower chances ongoing, especially across terrain. One "gotcha" to watch out for will be the potential for streamers to form off of Lake Champlain producing some higher elevation snow showers. Temperatures over the weekend may be cooler as well depending on cloud cover which may keep highs lower. Valley highs over the weekend are favored in the lower 40s, but could decrease into the upper 30s if clouds proliferate off of Lake Champlain given continued cool air advection. Lows will be in the 20s for most spots. KEY MESSAGE 2: The departing low will continue to pull away from the region Sunday, leading to continued northwesterly wrap-around flow with a few lingering showers. As the low exits, the depth of moisture will decrease throughout the day and shower coverage will further decrease from Saturday.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Our stretch of quieter weather gives way to a storm system bringing rain and mountain snow to Vermont and the North Country Thursday. A Winter Weather Advisory is in effect from 10 a.m. Thursday through 10 a.m. Friday for portions of the Adirondacks and southern Green Mountains. Snow showers may reach some valley floors Thursday night, though most lower elevations should see little to no accumulation. Tonight will be mostly cloudy with a low of 35°. Rain and mountain snow begin Thursday morning, with a high of 43°. As temperatures fall Thursday evening, snow levels will drop, allowing a mix or snow showers to reach some valleys overnight. The low will be 32°, with mountain snow showers lingering into early Friday. Friday will turn mostly sunny with a high of 41°. A few scattered valley mix and mountain snow showers are possible Friday night, with a low of 34°. Showers remain possible Saturday, mainly as rain in the valleys and snow in the mountains, with a high of 42° and a low of 37°. A few showers may linger Sunday, especially in the mountains, with a high of 44° and a low of 37°. High pressure brings a quieter start to next week. Monday will be partly sunny with a high of 44° and a low of 32°. Tuesday will be mostly sunny with a high of 46° and a low of 34°, followed by more sunshine and a high near 51° Wednesday.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-11T00:10:00Z — same caveat): Quiet Veterans Day, rain and snow arrive Thursday — Wednesday (Veterans Day) looks mostly dry, with only a spot shower or flurry possible. However, it will be mostly cloudy and chilly, with highs in the upper 40s. The late-week stretch looks quite chilly, as the jet stream dips farther south. Highs only reach the low to mid-40s, with lots of clouds. Rain and elevation snow showers develop Thursday, especially by afternoon, as an area of low pressure approaches. A period of steadier rain and mountain snow is likely Thursday night into Friday, with sprinkles and flurries lingering into Saturday. Several inches of snow will fall in southern parts of the region, higher up. Drier and brighter weather is likely next week, followed by a warmup into the 50s.
